Brief: Tell me about the Antikythera mechanism and how it was decoded. — about Design

1. The original mechanism apparently came out of the Mediterranean as a single encrusted piece.
2. Soon afterwards it fractured into three major pieces.
3. Other small pieces have broken off in the interim from cleaning and handling, and others were found on the sea floor by the Cousteau expedition.
4. Other fragments may still be in storage, undiscovered since their initial recovery; Fragment F was discovered in that way in 2005.
5. Of the 82 known fragments, seven are mechanically significant and contain the majority of the mechanism and inscriptions.
6. Another 16 smaller parts contain fractional and incomplete inscriptions.
7. Many of the smaller fragments that have been found contain nothing of apparent value, but a few have inscriptions on them.
8. Fragment 19 contains significant back door inscriptions including one reading "...
9. 76 years ..." which refers to the Callippic cycle.
10. Other inscriptions seem to describe the function of the back dials.
11. In addition to this important minor fragment, 15 further minor fragments have remnants of inscriptions on them.
